summary.text: King Quan travel token is a rough San Cha mountain token that lets a Gu Master exit King Quan Inheritance.

claims.text: Inside King Quan Inheritance, Fang Yuan finds the token as the hyena path reward once that pack vanishes. Corpse dogs and Yin dogs still hold the other two fog paths, with white silver relic Gu and two tasks at once Gu as their listed prizes. The token looks ordinary and rough, irregularly shaped, with a casual, ugly carving of San Cha Mountain on the surface. He drops interest in those two prizes to take it, judging it one of the best items there, later worth as much as a rank four Gu near the end of the three kings inheritance in his previous life.
When all three fog paths show dog groups and he cannot advance safely, he grips the token, bites his tongue, spits blood onto it, and speaks “Woof.” The token flares, tears space, and drags him out.
He appears in a bamboo forest on the northern side of San Cha mountain while the yellow King Quan light pillar still marks that inheritance’s entrance.

After that exit, the unsightly King Quan token already shows several deep cracks. King Quan travel token can be used three times at most. After three uses it cracks completely into pieces and cannot be used again. Those retreats are precious both as survival and as psychological room to choose paths more freely inside the inheritance.
